label: Reconstructed settler's working dress about 1810 (coarse unbleached shirt, blue neckerchief, brown waistcoat, loose linen trousers, shoes, a black round hat) on the shared portable male rig
basis: Original shells offset from the cleared adult body's own surface (the 1835 labourer's shirt, waistcoat and trousers, re-measured), a neckerchief lofted round its neck and a round hat rigid on the head, after the rural and working dress of 1811-15 in the recipe's pictures. Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing. The loose linen seat bridges the anatomical rear cleft with a reconstructed posterior section envelope and 12 mm extra ease, faded away at the waistband, upper thighs and outer hips; this is a garment-cut choice, not a body alteration or measured historical pattern.
source_scope: Krimmel's Black sawyers before the Bank of Pennsylvania (1811-13) show working men in shirt-sleeves, waistcoats, trousers and black round hats; his country inn (1811-13) rural men's dress; the Pixler family (about 1815) a rural American father's; Quaife (1913) that the settlers were armed as militia from the garrison store in their own clothes. No source describes any Chicago settler's or Black Jim's clothes in 1812; no pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

reference_summary.name: a settler or working man of Chicago, about 1810

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 adult-male graphical body and the shared generic skin of the period studies are reconstructed authoring choices. The figure is anonymous: a working man of the type, not any man of the town; no complexion, height, face or outfit of anyone is asserted.

settler_components.evidence_choice: The coordinator asked for people-1812-3466's settler_1812: plain farm clothes of about 1810 (shirt, waistcoat, trousers, neckerchief, a round or slouch hat, shoes), light on geometry, on the 1835 labourer as the near model. The labourer's braces are left out (one draw and 2,200 triangles fewer); the waistcoat is closed to the chest rather than open; the hat is the round black hat the Philadelphia sawyers wear. The same dress serves Black Jim (black_servant_1812: shirt, waistcoat, linen trousers, round black hat; no livery). The militia's musket and belts are carried things, not the dress.

provenance.source_scope: A coarse unbleached shirt with full sleeves, worn without a coat in August: Krimmel's sawyers (1811-13) work in shirt-sleeves; the colour (unbleached tow or linen) and cut (the 1835 labourer's) are reconstructed. No source describes a Chicago settler's clothes.
A kerchief at the neck (people-1812-3466: "open at the neck or with a kerchief"); blue cotton is our choice among the checks and colours of the period pictures.
A waistcoat over the shirt (the sawyers wear striped and green ones; the Pixler father a yellow one); brown wool, closed to the chest, is reconstructed.
Loose linen or tow trousers to the instep (the sawyers' trousers; people-1812-3466); natural colour and cut reconstructed.
A black round hat (the sawyers wear "black round hats"); a low round crown and a soft brim dipping a little fore and aft (the 1835 labourer's hat re-measured), reconstructed.
Shoes on the shared closed shoe; moccasins or bare feet in summer are equally likely and are not modelled.
